review.title: Player state machine
review.acceptance: The machine models the session and candidate lifecycle (resolving, loading a candidate, playing, buffering, seeking, recovering, failing over, ended, fatal) rather than UI state, which the controls layer already owns; the video element and the playback engine stay authoritative and the machine is a validated projection of them, so every engine and media event has an inbound transition even in states where it supposedly cannot occur. MANDATORY CONSOLIDATION, added 2026-09-18 by gpt-architect's round-48 direction when it approved PL-0903 and PL-0904. The reviewer was explicit that these are NOT reasons to reopen either of those tasks: PL-0502 owns the whole player surface and finishes the consolidation while implementing the machine. (1) RENAME browser_unsupported to an engine-neutral lifecycle reason, host_unsupported, as a COMPLETE migration -- type member, controller, machine, tests, reason trail, docs and comments -- with NO alias kept. One lifecycle fact gets one name. Behaviour is unchanged: the engine loaded and ran far enough to determine that the current host cannot support it. (2) TIGHTEN EngineState's unavailable variant from `detail?: EngineUnavailableDetail` to `detail: EngineUnavailableDetail | null`. Every producer must state whether detail was established; omission must not be the unknown representation. This is the same required-and-nullable discipline the contracts already apply to licenseUrl and to media facts. (3) UNIFY the duplicate engine-id vocabularies. PlaybackEngineId and PlaybackErrorEngine describe the same two values. Make one authoritative and derive or alias the other in the dependency-safe direction the code comments already identify. Two independently editable literal unions for one engine identity must not remain. (4) DO NOT WEAKEN PL-0904 while integrating: never make native code/category `number | null`; do not flatten mpvError into Shaka-numbered fields; do not invent a native failure classification without evidence; keep aborted engine control flow out of candidate failure accounting. (5) PRESERVE the existing no-clock/deterministic state-machine discipline and the bounded failover policy already present in playback-machine.ts.

review.title: Provider and URL security review
review.acceptance: A findings register exists at docs/SECURITY_REVIEW_PROVIDER_URL.md enumerating every finding across the five named classes -- SSRF, secret exposure, redirect handling, allowlist enforcement, and rights bypass -- each with a disposition of RESOLVED (with the commit and the test that now fails without the fix) or ACCEPTED (with the reason, the residual risk, and who accepted it). AN EMPTY REGISTER IS NOT A PASS. The register must state, per class, what was examined and by what method, so that 'no finding' is distinguishable from 'not looked for'; a class examined by reading alone must say so rather than implying a test covered it. Every RESOLVED entry needs a regression that fails against the pre-fix tree, because a security fix without a test that would have caught the bug is indistinguishable from a refactor. Every ACCEPTED entry that touches credentials, licensing or an irreversible production change is an escalation under control/policies.json escalation.humanOnly and may NOT be accepted by an agent; it is recorded as OPEN-ESCALATED and named in the handoff. Out of scope and to be listed as such rather than silently skipped: anything requiring a real licensed provider or live credentials (PL-0302, PL-0602), and the desktop sidecar trust boundary already ruled on in PL-0901 and reviewed under PL-0501.
review.acceptanceSupersededAtClaim: SSRF, secret exposure, redirect, allowlist, and rights-bypass findings are resolved or explicitly accepted
review.acceptanceAmendedBeforeClaim: AMENDED 2026-09-17 BY claude-lead, BEFORE THE CLAIM, AND NOT AT A REVIEWER'S REQUEST -- flagged to gpt-architect for confirmation rather than treated as settled. The original clause, preserved verbatim in acceptanceSupersededAtClaim, was: 'SSRF, secret exposure, redirect, allowlist, and rights-bypass findings are resolved or explicitly accepted'. That sentence is satisfied by an agent reporting that it found nothing, which under invariant 8 is the shape of a fabricated gate rather than a passed one: the only two gates on this task are security-review and rights-review, both judgement gates, and neither has a command whose exit code can contradict a wrong answer. The amendment does not lower the bar or narrow the scope -- the same five classes, the same surface -- it makes the existing bar falsifiable, by requiring the method to be published alongside the conclusion and by refusing an empty register as evidence. If the reviewer considers a pre-claim acceptance amendment by the implementing lead improper even in the stricter direction, this is the record to point at, and the original clause is recoverable from the field above.

review.title: A real catalog metadata source
review.notes: The discovery layer has no metadata source. PL-0105 landed a seam, and docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md says so in its first line; this task is the thing that belongs behind it, tracked so the gap stays visible instead of being hidden by a port that looks finished. docs/PRODUCT_SPEC.md step 2 of the initial user journey is browse/search normalized metadata, and nothing in this repository ingests any: every surface reads six fictional works. PL-0301 and PL-0302 do not close it - they supply stream candidates, which is what a title plays from, not what a catalog is made of. PARTLY BLOCKED, and the split is deliberate rather than a hedge. The design half - identity and dedupe, refresh and staleness, tombstones, paging, provider-side search, the locale-tagged contract, and the undeclared-rights state that catalogItemSchema cannot currently express - needs no external access and can begin now. Connecting an actual metadata provider, and carrying artwork, cannot: both need an agreement and credentials, which control/policies.json escalates to human-only under Licensing and Credentials - the same categories that block PL-0302. It is a DIFFERENT agreement from PL-0302's, covering catalog metadata and image rights rather than stream rights, so this is not merely waiting on that task; the honest status is BACKLOG with the ceiling named, not BLOCKED on someone else's licence.
review.acceptance: A metadata source stands behind resolveCatalogMetadataSource and answers what the port deliberately does not. Ingestion: something fetches, schedules and backfills, rather than an array being maintained by hand. Refresh: an answer carries its age and a stated staleness policy, so nobody has to guess how old a rail is. Identity and dedupe: how a provider's native id becomes a normalizedContentId, and what happens when two sources describe the same work, is settled as a design decision before it is coded - this is the largest missing piece and it is not a coding question. Deletion: a work that disappears from a source produces a tombstone, so it stays distinguishable from a fetch that failed. Paging and provider-side search: listRecords returning everything is a shape only six fixtures can use, and who owns ranking and paging is part of the contract rather than an accident of in-memory filtering. Artwork: images arrive with their own licensing, tracked separately from the work's, or they do not arrive. Localization and availability: title, genre and synopsis are locale-tagged and a work can be offered in more than one language, and availability windows and territory exist, so the empty state's claim about a region is backed by something. Every record declares a rights basis whose category agrees with its item and whose reference is an opaque internal identifier or null, and the ingestion path is treated as untrusted third-party I/O - allowlisted egress, bounded bodies, redirects revalidated, and no media address anywhere in a catalog payload.

THE COMMANDER'S LICENSING DECISION IS NOW IMPLEMENTED: Wikidata stands behind resolveCatalogMetadataProvider, which closes the first acceptance clause that round 44 correctly refused to claim. The port did not move -- wikidata.ts imports FROM provider.ts and nothing in the port imports back, and ingest, project, identity, freshness and safety never mention Wikidata -- which is what keeps the decision an INITIAL source choice rather than a shape baked into the seam. CAPABILITIES ARE DECLARED HONESTLY RATHER THAN OPTIMISTICALLY, each measured: providerSideSearch true; incrementalSince FALSE because WDQS's default graph binds nothing for schema:version or dateModified and the Action API that has them costs a measured 206 KB per entity, so changedSince is ignored entirely rather than silently approximated; reportsDeletions FALSE because deletions need a different API; maxPageSize 50, the number the source itself uses; and sourceRevision ALWAYS NULL, which is a real gap stated as one -- a consumer cannot tell whether a record changed between passes. Enumeration is keyset-paged on the numeric QID rather than OFFSET, because CirrusSearch hard-fails at offset 10,000, measured. THE CC0 / CC BY-SA DISTINCTION IS ENFORCED BY FOUR MECHANICAL CONTROLS, NOT DOCUMENTED: a frozen two-host set with construction refused if the operator's egress allowlist names anything else, so en.wikipedia.org in the policy yields NO provider; an entity-id pattern admitting only Q, P and L, with Commons M-ids refused by name; no SERVICE clause in any built query, asserted; and no request for P18, P154, P3383, sitelinks or extracts, with artwork always empty and unable to be otherwise. THE USER-AGENT OBLIGATION IS STRUCTURAL: the option stays required with no default, createWikidataProvider additionally refuses an agent string with no contact token or with a browser token by two separate named refusals, and a ts-expect-error test fails if a default is ever added -- a bad agent gets no provider rather than an IP block. RIGHTS MACHINERY ON REAL RECORDS: the rights register is required with no default and noRightsBasisEstablished must be passed BY NAME, so a default composition against real Wikidata publishes NOTHING, asserted over three recorded real films -- that is the correct outcome, not a bug. P6216 is read and not interpreted. The pre-parse media-address scan now has an untrusted writer behind it, since a Wikidata label is editable by anyone logged in and a vandalised title reading like a manifest URL is an ordinary string to the schema; the test is built from a real response with one label replaced. A FINDING THE IMPLEMENTER GOT BY WRITING THE TEST AND GETTING THE OTHER ANSWER: a rights reference carrying a contract URL is refused as media_address_in_catalog_payload rather than as a non-opaque reference, because the address scan runs first. ROUND 44'S TRIPWIRE FIRED AND WAS INVERTED RATHER THAN DELETED: the licensed-source set is frozen, holds only wikidata, throws on runtime mutation and licenses no keyed source, and a tmdb request is refused by name. LIVE TESTS ARE OUT OF THE GATE: wikidata.live.test.ts hits the real service, is excluded by the package vitest config, reachable only through a separate script, and was run deliberately -- 3 passed in 20.4s -- but is not what this gate rests on.

notCoveredByThisDecision: Any credentialed source. TMDB and anything else requiring an API key remains a separate Credentials escalation and is untouched by this.
Whether bulk ingestion engages the EU/UK sui generis database right. That question applies to Wikidata as much as to any other candidate and is for counsel, not for this record.
Commercial use terms for any future source. Only Wikidata's CC0 position on structured data was evidenced.
licensingDecision.obligationsThatFollow: Wikidata's structured data is CC0, but access is not unconditional: the Wikimedia User-Agent policy requires an informative User-Agent with contact information or the client may be IP-blocked without notice, and browser-impersonating agents are forbidden. That is why CatalogDocumentOptions.userAgent is required with no default, and it must stay that way. Text outside the main, property and lexeme namespaces is CC BY-SA rather than CC0, so the distinction has to survive into whatever is ingested.

review.title: An agent instruction file has provenance, or it is not an instruction
review.acceptance: Repository validation detects any AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md under a working directory that is not on an explicit, reviewed allowlist, and the authoritative instruction hierarchy is stated somewhere an agent reads before it starts. THE CONCRETE CASE: apps/web/AGENTS.md is GENERATED BY next dev and instructs agents to read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code. Nothing acted on it, and it is almost certainly benign. The finding is not that file -- it is that framework tooling can write an instruction file into a directory agents treat as authoritative, which makes a dependency's postinstall a path into the control plane's instruction surface. Required: the allowlist names each legitimate instruction file and who owns it, so an unowned one is a validation failure rather than a judgement call; generated instruction files are either gitignored and removed or allowlisted after being read, and the choice is recorded per file; validation fails on an unexpected file rather than warning, because a warning in a passing run is not a control; a regression plants an unexpected AGENTS.md and observes the failure, since a detector nobody has seen fire is not known to work; and the instruction hierarchy is written down -- which file wins, and that nothing under node_modules is ever authoritative. WHAT THIS TASK MUST NOT DO: silently delete a file a framework needs, or treat allowlisting as review. An allowlisted generated file must have been READ by a human or an agent that reports what it says.
review.notes: Created 2026-09-18 on gpt-architect's round-46 instruction, reviewing PL-0702 at bbfaa5a997e6ee146271f26e5b2546b7e67e47d2. This one came out of the PL-0702 subagent flagging the file rather than acting on it, which is the behaviour the instruction-source boundary asks for; the reviewer agreed it is a real control-plane supply-chain surface and directed that it NOT block PL-0502. recommended.title: Contract module boundaries
recommended.acceptance: Shared vocabularies live in their own leaf modules, domain contracts live in one module each, index.ts is a re-export-only compatibility barrel rather than the authoritative public surface, and a wildcard exports map lets a new domain contract be added without touching package metadata or the barrel; no cycle-driven z.lazy remains and structural regressions prove the boundary rather than merely reflecting it; no schema behaviour changes

recommended.title: Profile model
recommended.acceptance: Profiles are modelled above authentication rather than inside the auth library, with the active profile carried alongside the session rather than inside the identity record; profile scoping is present in the first migration rather than retrofitted, because that is the part that is expensive to reverse; profiles can be created and selected with authorization tests

recommended.title: Provider health contract
recommended.acceptance: A provider with zero observations reports unknown with a null observed success rate and a zero sample count, never a mid-range score and never a pass; any prior used to rank an unobserved provider is labelled as a prior rather than presented as measured availability; degraded-but-usable is a state distinct from up and down; health output is pure over the observations plus an explicit policy version, with no hidden wall-clock decay; and health never affects entitlement, so a provider at perfect health still cannot make an unauthorized candidate eligible

recommended.title: Fixture provider states the protection fact it actually knows
recommended.acceptance: The fixture provider adapter emits contentProtection { state: "clear" } for its own candidates, because for a fixture the absence of DRM is a fact the adapter genuinely knows rather than something it is guessing. Created from gpt-architect's round-44 non-blocking finding on PL-0501, in the reviewer's own words: "Create a provider-owned task for the fixture provider protection fact. The fixture adapter, not PL-0501, should emit { state: \"clear\" } when that fact is genuinely known. PL-0501 may keep PROTECTION_NOT_STATED as the conservative fallback until that provider task lands." So the deliverable is a narrowing of where the fact is asserted, not a behaviour change in routing: PROTECTION_NOT_STATED stays in PL-0501 as the fallback for every adapter that has not stated a protection fact, and this task removes the fixture from the set that needs it. Required, and each is a way this task could be done wrongly: the fixture must set the field itself rather than PL-0501 special-casing the fixture provider id, because a consumer branching on a provider identity is exactly the provider-specific logic outside @liberty/provider-sdk that invariant 3 forbids; requiresContentDecryptionModule must be observed returning false for a fixture candidate and the observation recorded, since state !== "clear" is the whole point of the encoding and an untested clear is indistinguishable from an untested unknown; the fallback path in PL-0501 must be left in place and a test must still cover an adapter that states nothing, because deleting the fallback once its only current user stops needing it would fail open for the next adapter; and no other adapter may be given a protection fact here, because for a real provider the honest value is unknown and asserting clear for one would be a rights misstatement rather than a defaulting decision. Out of scope: any change to contract shape (PL-0902 owns it), to ranking (@liberty/media-engine), or to capability routing.
recommended.notes: Provenance: gpt-architect CHANGES_REQUESTED on PL-0501, reviewed at 27d3a03389781256451c5e52d72520132cfa76c1, non-blocking/follow-up section.
